newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RESEACH ALERT - BIL raised to "accumulate".
newsitem.headline: RESEACH ALERT - BIL raised to "accumulate".

text.p: Cavill White Securities said it had upgraded its recommendation on Brierley Investments Ltd to "accumulate" from "hold" after its first-half profit result published earlier this month.
"Brierley's portfolio of assets is better positioned than it has been for some time, both in terms of liquidity and diversification," analyst Dave Copley said in a research paper dated March 6.
"Brierley's 'thorn' of the past, Thistle Hotels, has been partially removed," he said.
BIL's first half net profit fell to NZ$116.1 million from $170 million a year earlier due to only $6 million of investment profits being realised, $75 million less than the prior period.
While BIL still holds 46 percent of Thistle, Copley said this holding was now more liquid (being listed) and the outlook for Thistle's share price was positive.
He said BIL was now clearly focused on Australasian capital markets in which it had a competitive advantage and the 'corporate raider' role largely to itself.
It also had substantial balance sheet capacity to invest, as shown by its purchase of 20 percent in media group John Fairfax Holdings.
Cavill White forecast a full year profit to June 1997 of $303.0 million for BIL.

Cavill White said it currently values BIL ordinary shares at $1.48 and the convertible notes at $1.37. On Thursday the shares were down two cents at $1.34 and the notes up one at $1.26. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
